Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 1) Rational use of medicine means patients receive drugs according to clinical need, in individual dose, for adequate period and at:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option2: Lowest cost to patient and community
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational use emphasizes clinical need, correct dose and adequate duration. Cost is also important. The aim is effective treatment with minimum unnecessary burden.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 2) The short formula for rational use of medicines is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option1: Right tablet size + Right smell + Right advertisement
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option2: Right patient + Right drug + Right dose + Right duration + Lowest cost
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option3: Right route + Right packaging + Right price only
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option4: Right brand + Right colour + Right company
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational use means selecting drug properly for the patient. Dose and duration must be appropriate. Cost should be reasonable for patient and community.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 3) One criterion of rational prescribing is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: A drug should be prescribed only when there is a proper indication. Unnecessary prescribing increases harm and cost. Indication is the first major criterion.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 4) The first step in rational prescribing is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Diagnosis should come before drug selection. Even if final diagnosis is not confirmed, a provisional diagnosis is needed. Without diagnosis, treatment becomes irrational.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 5) After establishing diagnosis, the next step is to define the:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Therapeutic problem means the condition needing treatment. Examples include pain, infection or hypertension. This helps guide drug selection logically.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 6) Therapeutic goals should be defined before:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Therapeutic goal means what we want to achieve. It may be symptom relief, cure or prevention of complications. Drug selection should match that goal.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 7) After defining the therapeutic goal, the prescriber should select the:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option2: Drug class capable of achieving the goal
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: First choose the appropriate drug class. Then select the specific drug from that class. This prevents random prescribing.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 8) Specific drug selection should be based on:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: ESSC is a key prescribing principle. A drug should work, be safe, suit the patient and be affordable. This is one of the most important rational prescribing points.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 9) Dose, route and duration should be decided according to:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Dose, route and duration must be individualized. Age, weight, pregnancy, renal/hepatic disease and severity matter. Fixed prescribing for all patients is unsafe.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 10) Clear patient instructions mainly improve:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Patients must understand dose, timing and duration. Clear instructions reduce misuse. Good explanation improves adherence.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 11) Monitoring adherence means checking whether the patient is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Adherence means following the prescribed plan. Poor adherence can cause treatment failure or toxicity. Monitoring helps detect and correct the problem.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 12) Monitoring during rational prescribing should assess therapeutic response and:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Monitoring should check both benefit and harm. Therapeutic response shows whether the goal is achieved. ADR monitoring detects toxicity early.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 13) Treatment should be modified when:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option1: Goals are not achieved or adverse effects occur
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational prescribing is not finished after writing the prescription. Response and adverse effects must be reviewed. Treatment should be changed if needed.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 14) Irrational prescribing is a major cause of:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Irrational antibiotic use promotes AMR. Wrong drug, wrong dose or unnecessary antibiotics increase resistance. This is a major public health problem.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 15) A common example of irrational prescribing is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Polypharmacy means unnecessary use of multiple drugs. It increases interaction and ADR risk. It also increases cost and confusion.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 16) Direct consequence of irrational medicine use includes:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Irrational treatment may fail to control disease. Wrong drug, dose or duration can delay cure. This increases morbidity and patient suffering.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 17) Irrational prescribing may increase:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Irrational prescribing exposes patients to unnecessary harm. It increases adverse reactions and hospitalization. It also creates financial loss.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 18) Lowest cost in rational use refers to cost to:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational use considers both individual and public cost. A drug should be affordable and effective. Unnecessary expensive therapy is irrational when safer cheaper options exist.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 19) Correct dispensing is a criterion of:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Correct drug must be dispensed in correct amount and form. Dispensing error can make a good prescription unsafe. Rational use includes prescribing and dispensing.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 20) Adequate monitoring is important because it detects:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Monitoring checks whether the drug is working. It also detects adverse drug reactions. This is essential for safe long-term therapy.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 21) “Appropriate patient” means the prescribed drug should consider:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Patient factors include age, pregnancy, lactation and organ disease. Renal, hepatic and G6PD cautions are important. The same drug may be suitable for one patient but unsafe for another.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 22) ESSC stands for:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: ESSC is the key principle for selecting a specific drug. The drug should be effective and safe. It should also suit the patient and be affordable.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 23) Irrational prescribing may lead to loss of:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Treatment failure and adverse effects reduce trust. Patients may lose confidence in health care. This is one of the listed impacts of irrational prescribing.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 24) Which prescription is most rational?
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option1: Antibiotic for every fever without assessment
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option2: Drug chosen after diagnosis, correct dose, clear advice and follow-up
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option3: Multiple drugs given to impress patient
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational prescribing starts with diagnosis. Drug, dose, route and duration must be appropriate. Clear instructions and monitoring complete the process.

Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.question: 25) The most accurate statement is:
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option1: Cost is irrelevant in rational drug use
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option2: Rational prescribing ends after writing prescription
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option3: Good prescribing requires diagnosis, ESSC-based drug choice, instructions and monitoring
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.option4: Monitoring is needed only for antibiotics
Rational Use of Drugs and Rational presc.exp: Rational prescribing is a full process. It includes diagnosis, therapeutic goal, drug choice and individualized dosing. Patient instructions, adherence and ADR monitoring are also essential.
